_**User (2026-10-09 23:51:20Z)**_

I am trying to install strykerjs and I am asked, is this project using one of the frameworks? I know it's not angular-cli, svelte, or vue, but should I say create-react-app?

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-09 23:51:30Z)**_

**No, pick "None/other".** Actual Budget doesn't use create-react-app. The frontend (`desktop-client`) is built with **Vite**, and every package runs its tests with **Vitest**. The CRA preset sets Stryker up to use Jest through `react-scripts`, and this repo has neither, so that config would fail as soon as you ran it.

For the next prompts:

- **Test runner:** choose **vitest**. That installs `@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner`.
- **Reporters:** pick whatever you like. `html` and `clear-text` are the usual choices.
- **Package manager:** choose **yarn**. Note that Stryker's init installs packages with plain yarn commands, and Yarn 4 workspaces can be picky about that. If the install step fails, add the packages yourself from the repo root, in the workspace you're testing:
  ```bash
  yarn workspace @actual-app/core add -D @stryker-mutator/core @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner
  ```

This repo is a monorepo, so point Stryker at one package rather than the whole repo. `packages/loot-core` is a good place to start because it holds most of the business logic and unit tests. Put the Stryker config in that package and limit the files it mutates with the `mutate` setting, for example `src/server/budget/**/*.ts`. Mutation testing all of loot-core in one run would take a very long time.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-09 23:52:14Z)**_

**Leave it empty.** Vitest compiles the TypeScript on the fly when it runs, so nothing needs to be built first. loot-core's test scripts confirm this: `test:node` is just `vitest --run` and `test:web` is `vitest --run -c vitest.web.config.ts`, with no build or pretest step ([packages/loot-core/package.json:185-187](packages/loot-core/package.json#L185-L187)).

There's one thing to set after init finishes. loot-core has two Vitest configs, and Stryker should use the main one. Add this to the generated Stryker config:

```json
"vitest": { "configFile": "vitest.config.ts" }
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-09 23:52:36Z)**_

**Keep the defaults (html, clear-text, progress) and press Enter.**

- **html** writes a report you open in your browser, at `reports/mutation/mutation.html` by default. You can click through each file and see which mutants survived. This is the most useful one.
- **clear-text** prints a summary table in the terminal when the run finishes.
- **progress** shows a progress bar while it runs, which helps because mutation runs can take a long time.
- **dashboard**: leave it off. It uploads your results to the public Stryker Dashboard website and needs an API token, so it isn't worth setting up for a class project.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-09 23:53:16Z)**_

**Choose yarn.** This repo uses Yarn 4, and choosing npm would create a stray `package-lock.json` and could break `node_modules`.

If the install step fails (Yarn 4 workspaces can reject the command Stryker runs), that's fine because the config file still gets written. Install the packages yourself from the repo root:

```bash
yarn workspace @actual-app/core add -D @stryker-mutator/core @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner
```

If you ran `stryker init` from the repo root instead of `packages/loot-core`, the packages may land in the root `package.json`. Tell me and I'll help you move them.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-09 23:53:25Z)**_

**Choose JSON.** You'll get a `stryker.config.json` that's easy to read and edit, and VS Code will autocomplete the settings from Stryker's schema. You'd only need the JavaScript option to compute settings in code, and you won't need that here.

Once it's written, add the two settings from earlier:

```json
"vitest": { "configFile": "vitest.config.ts" },
"mutate": ["src/server/budget/**/*.ts", "!src/**/*.test.ts"]
```

Change the `mutate` paths to whichever part of loot-core you want to test.
